extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants to JSPS KAKENHI (Grants‑in‑Aid for Scientific Research) and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Official description of how JSPS conducts peer review for KAKENHI proposals, including review sections, review methods (Comprehensive vs Two‑Stage), use of solicited written comments and interviews, and links to category‑specific assessment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of review: Research Proposal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: The review for KAKENHI is carried out by the Scientific Research Grant Committee of the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), and it is based on the Research Proposal Document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proposal assessment is founded on the submitted Research Proposal Document; reviewers examine and judge proposals using the document as the primary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of reviewers / committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee consists of approximately 8,000 reviewers who have been selected from each academic field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review assignments and judgments are made by this large, field‑diverse committee; reviewer expertise is matched to research fields via the review sectioning system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Section (KAKENHI Review Section Table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for proposals and proposal review are conducted in accordance with the 'KAKENHI Review Section Table' consisting of 'Basic Sections', 'Medium-sized Sections', and 'Broad Sections' (the former detailed List of Categories, Areas, Disciplines and Research Fields has been abolished).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are classified into these review sections which determine how proposals are assigned and evaluated; applicants should select the appropriate section when applying because it affects reviewer matching and review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Method: Comprehensive Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal review for the categories Scientific Research (S/A), Scientific Research (B/C) (application section 'Generative Research Fields'), and Challenging Research (Pioneering/Exploratory) is conducted by the method of 'Comprehensive Review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will conduct document reviews on all research proposals, and the same reviewer will conduct a discussion from a broad perspective on each research proposal at panel reviews. Implies both individual document assessment and panel discussion by the same reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Method: Two-Stage Document Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal review for the categories Scientific Research (B/C) (application section 'General') and Early Career Scientists is carried out by the method of 'Two-Stage Document Review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will conduct document reviews in two stages and Panel reviews will not be conducted. Implies an initial screening stage followed by a secondary document assessment without panel deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of solicited external written comments (Specially Promoted & Scientific Research (S))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each proposal submitted to the categories Specially Promoted Research and Scientific Research (S), a few researchers in the relevant field of specialization are solicited for written comments, which are utilized in document reviews and panel reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External specialist written comments supplement committee reviewers' evaluations; applicants in these categories should expect targeted solicitation of expert opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview at final review stage (Specially Promoted & Scientific Research (S))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview of the applicant will be conducted at the final review stage for certain categories (Specially Promoted Research and Scientific Research (S)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final selection for these categories may include an applicant interview in addition to document and panel review; performance in the interview can affect final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment Criteria for Document Review (FY2025) — category‑specific documents
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS provides detailed 'Assessment Criteria for Document Review (FY2025)' for each research category (linked PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category‑specific assessment criteria exist and are published as PDFs for: Grant‑in‑Aid for Scientific Research (S); Grant‑in‑Aid for Scientific Research (A) (General); Grant‑in‑Aid for Scientific Research (B/C) (General); Grant‑in‑Aid for Early‑Career Scientists; Grant‑in‑Aid for Challenging Research (Pioneering/Exploratory); Grant‑in‑Aid for Research Activity Start‑up (FY2024); International Leading Research (FY2023); Fostering Joint International Research (FY2024). Applicants should consult the relevant PDF for the precise scoring criteria and itemized guidance for their category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and disclosure of review results
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of the review results is made to the applicants via their affiliated research institutions; selected projects are posted on the KAKEN database. Principal Investigators whose proposals were not selected and who wish to request disclosure can request information; JSPS is planning to disclose the approximate ranking per the review section via the electronic application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive institutional notification; public posting provides transparency for selected projects; non-selected applicants may request further information (approximate ranking) through official channels.
